newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: New Zealand's Brierley raises Fairfax stake.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand's Brierley raises Fairfax stake.

text.p: New Zealand investment group Brierley Investments Ltd said on Thursday it had boosted its stake in Australia's oldest newspaper publisher, John Fairfax Holdings Ltd, to 22 percent after acquiring another two percent.

Brierley's subsidiary, Australian Consolidated Investments Ltd, said in a shareholder notice to the Australian Stock Exchange that it had bought 16 million Fairfax shares for a total of A$51.9 million (US$38.9 million) in recent days.
Prior to this latest share purchases, the Brierley group held 19.98 percent of Fairfax or 151.53 million shares.
Brierley became Fairfax's largest shareholder when it bought the bulk of the 25 percent formerly held by Canadian media baron Conrad Black last December.
A disappointed Black sold out after he was blocked by the Australian government from raising his stake to make his control of Fairfax more secure from predators.

Although the government is reviewing cross media ownership laws which prevent a television station owner from owning a major newspaper in the same market, it made clear it would not lift restrictions on foreign ownership of media.
The government's stance boosted talk that Australia's richest man, Kerry Packer, would bid for Fairfax if he was freed from the cross-media constraints.

Packer has long made clear that he wants to acquire Fairfax to add to his television and magazine interests. His media group Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd owns 15 percent of Fairfax, the maximum permitted under cross-media rules.
But any Packer bid succeeding would depend on Brierley accepting the offer.
Brierley has said it has no plans to sell its Fairfax stake in the short term.
The New Zealand investment group is allowed to increase its Fairfax stake by three percent every six months under local stock exchange rules.
Separately, a spokeswoman for the Australian Securities Commission said the ASC was examining recent share trades in Fairfax.
She said the examination was a preliminary inquiry and was not a formal investigation.
Fairfax shares closed two cents up at A$3.20 with just over one million shares traded on Thursday.
Brierley paid an average of A$3.24 per Fairfax share for its purchases over the past 10 days.
